views.title: The pipeline
views.lede: How a plan is built, shaped, explained, read for load and adapted, and where the numbers come from.

nodes.label: Goal and baseline
nodes.note: The goal profile, target date, baseline (recent time, weekly volume, experience, age), available days, kit and schedule.

nodes.label: Onboarding
nodes.note: Collects the goal and baseline and posts the plan request.

nodes.label: Engine generation
nodes.note: Deterministic: the phase arc, the weekly volume and long-run curve, VDOT paces, and every session. It computes every number.

nodes.label: AI shaping pass
nodes.note: Reads the engine's plan and chooses typed intents only. An answer outside the set is dropped.

nodes.label: Stored plan
nodes.note: The goal, plan, weeks and sessions written to D1.

nodes.label: Reason pass
nodes.note: Rewords each session's reason after the plan is saved, in the background, and keeps the deterministic reason as the fallback.

nodes.label: Load model
nodes.note: Reads the plan and the runner's logs in shadow, and can only ease or hold a future week.

nodes.label: Adapt
nodes.note: Rebuilds only the weeks that have not started, seeded with real recent volume and feedback.

nodes.label: UI surfaces
nodes.note: Today, Week, Coach and Progress render the stored plan and convert units at the edge.

edges.label: typed intents, applied inside the engine's bounds
writes goal, plan, weeks and sessions

views.title: Rules and boundaries
views.lede: The boundaries everyone must hold, and every invariant with the test that keeps it true.

nodes.label: Units are presentation and the engine is unit-free
nodes.note: The engine computes in km and seconds per km; km/mi conversion and pace display happen at the edge from user settings. A stored prescription is metric.

nodes.label: The engine computes every number
nodes.note: A model never writes a distance, a pace or a count. The AI chooses typed intents only, and an out-of-set answer is dropped.

nodes.label: The load model may ease or hold and never build
nodes.note: No path may raise a week above the engine's own curve.

nodes.label: The roughly ten percent weekly ceiling holds
nodes.note: No positive step exceeds it; the two-week progression ceiling is about thirty percent.

nodes.label: A week's prescribed total must not exceed the week's own target
No ACWR threshold
nodes.note: Load is read as a trend; there is no ratio to cross.

nodes.label: No medical diagnosis
nodes.note: A health risk is redirected, never diagnosed (`coach-safety`).

nodes.label: Prefer data over code
nodes.note: A new goal or machine is data, not new logic. User preferences (units, week start) live in the `settings.prefs` JSON, not in new columns or branches.

nodes.label: Writing is a boundary too
nodes.note: Every user-facing string follows the human-writing rules (no em dashes, no AI tells, mono for data), including any prompt that produces visible text. See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) and the `human-writing` skill. Every prose model path carries `WRITING_RULES` in the prompt it sends and runs the reply through `sanitizeText` before it is stored or shown; the guard in `packages/shared/src/writing-guard.test.ts` finds the prose call sites and fails when one is missing them.

views.title: Why things are this way
views.lede: Each settled decision from the decision log, linked to its entry and its why.

nodes.label: Decision log
nodes.note: Every settled decision and its why, newest first.

nodes.label: Strength sessions are full-body with a lean, not split days
nodes.note: 2026-11-27. every generated strength session keeps a lower-body spine in a fixed priority order (a squat or leg-press pattern, a hip hinge, knee flexion, calf work), followed by the lean's extra move for its area and then one or two upper-body or core accessories. The day's focus adds to this spine rather than replacing it. With two weekly strength sessions both lean legs and hips (their first accessory alternating push and pull across the week); with three, two lean legs and hips and one leans upper body and core; a single scheduled strength day stays full-body with no lean. An upper-body accessory never displaces a lower-body pattern: the spine leads every sequence, so a short session (a heavy sport week trims the circuit to four moves) loses accessories before it loses leg patterns. A chosen heuristic keeps about two thirds or more of the working sets in the lower body, stated as a heuristic in the session's why. Lean days carry plain titles ("Leg day", "Upper body day") and whys in plain body-part words, with no "upper push" or "upper pull" jargon. Each why names only the accessory work the built circuit actually holds, so a session too short for an accessory says so instead of claiming whole-body work, and the why keeps the day honest about what it does carry. The phase arc follows the research too: the full requested count in base, at most two maintenance sessions through a race build and peak with a set cut and the load kept, one short session in the first taper week, and none in the final days before the race. When a phase asks for fewer sessions, the dropped strength day goes quiet (a rest day) instead of becoming more running, so the week's running days stay the same from the first week to the last. This supersedes "The week rotates the strength focus across the body" (2026-11-26): its focus vocabulary survives as the lean, but the layout it produced (a legs day, an upper push day, an upper pull day) concentrated most muscles into about one weekly exposure at the runner's two to three sessions. Its rule-out lines (the same circuit every day, a bodybuilding split that ignores running) still hold.

links.label: Strength sessions are full-body with a lean, not split days

nodes.label: Mobility anchors on the stated tight area and roams one stretch around it
nodes.note: 2026-11-27. a generated mobility session is composed in the engine instead of naming one library workout. The runner's voted focus (from their niggles, terrain and sports, at any flexibility gap) anchors the session: the same two static holds for that area at every session, two rounds of 30 to 45 seconds each, never shortened by rotation. One roaming stretch per session rotates through the other common runner areas along one shared order, so sessions and weeks differ while the tight area's dose stays fixed, and a stretch never roams twice before the whole order has cycled. When a week carries at least three composed sessions, one of them anchors on the runner-up vote instead (with no second vote, the next common runner area), while the stated focus keeps a clear majority of the composed work. A favorite mobility workout weights the rotation rather than overriding it: it takes every second session of the plan, so the composed variants still cycle through the weeks it does not take. Every stretch that targets a muscle counts toward that muscle's weekly dose, roaming overlaps included; a drill that is a movement rather than a hold stays in the dynamic warm-up and never counts as static dose; and nothing is scaled up past the static plateau of about ten minutes a week per target muscle, though lower weekly doses still produce gains. This annotates the earlier behaviour of aiming the mobility routine at the runner's stated areas: the aim stays, rotation is added around it.

links.label: Mobility anchors on the stated tight area and roams one stretch around it

nodes.label: CodeRabbit findings are applied by suggestion or backlogged, not hand-fixed
nodes.note: 2026-11-27. review findings are cleared in two ways, and the main session stops rewriting code in a loop for them. A comment that carries a suggested diff is applied verbatim (its suggestion action) after the diff is read and the gate passes; a comment CodeRabbit can fix itself is handed to it; and a finding we do not apply is recorded in `backlog/` with the reason and the source link. Only non-blocking findings are backlogged: a release-blocking one (a security hole, data loss, a broken auth path) is fixed before merge, whatever the review's severity tag says. Threads resolve against one of those two outcomes, and a PR merges with the review green and no comment left open (AGENTS.md "CodeRabbit review", backlog/README.md).

links.label: CodeRabbit findings are applied by suggestion or backlogged, not hand-fixed

nodes.label: Rest between strength sets is a band, and rest is an explicit card
nodes.note: 2026-11-27. the engine gives every strength move its rest from a phase band instead of a flat 75 seconds: 45 to 60 seconds in base, 75 to 90 in build, 90 to 120 in peak, with the runner's level nudging inside the band (a beginner at the short end, an advanced runner at the long end), snapped to five seconds. A plyometric move always takes at least 90 seconds so every contact stays sharp. A taper week keeps the build band and the post-race recovery weeks rest like the base. The rest is now an explicit step in the guided sequence (`kind: 'rest'`): one card after each set, where the card after a move's final set is the pause before the next move, and the final set of the final move runs straight into the cool-down, which stays rest-free. The player's implicit rest machinery is gone: the "Rest now" button and the countdown it armed are replaced by the rest card, which ticks by itself and can be extended 30 seconds at a time. The Skip rest control confirms first and names what skipping costs, while moving through the stage list passes a rest card with no prompt. The session's length estimate is the sum of its parts (drills, work at about four seconds a rep plus setup, and rest) instead of a flat 50 minutes. The detail page's "What's to come" list stays work-focused, one row per move, with rest cards visible only in the player's flow.

links.label: Rest between strength sets is a band, and rest is an explicit card

nodes.label: Plan warnings reach the runner
nodes.note: 2026-11-27. the engine's `meta.warnings` are stored on the plan's params at generation and shown on the plan overview as written, and the preview rebuild's warnings ride on the preview response and show in onboarding on the screens the runner lands on after the rebuild. This supersedes the follow-up note in "A mid-week start opens with a short week, and the week floor follows the goal and the runner", which said the rebuild warning is returned but not shown; it is shown now.

nodes.label: Every PR waits for a complete CodeRabbit review before merge
nodes.note: 2026-11-27. every PR gets a CodeRabbit review. After opening a PR, wait for the review rather than merging on the CI gate alone, by scheduling a wakeup instead of blocking the turn. Read the review comments yourself, resolve every addressable artifact (nitpicks, outside-diff comments, inline comments and review summaries), and merge only when the review is complete and clean and the CI gate passes. A subagent's PR follows the same rule.

links.label: Every PR waits for a complete CodeRabbit review before merge

nodes.label: The week rotates the strength focus across the body
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. a strength day leans on a focus (legs and hips, upper push, upper pull, core and stability) chosen by the session's position among the week's strength days, and the moves within a focus rotate by the session index. One strength day stays a full-body circuit, two split into legs and upper body, and three or more rotate legs, upper push, upper pull and core. The why names the focus.

links.label: The week rotates the strength focus across the body

nodes.label: The system map's selected view is component state, not a derive of the hash
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. the admin system map holds the selected view and node in component state, seeds them from the URL hash on mount, writes the hash with `replaceState` for the deep link, and reads the hash back through a `hashchange` listener. It no longer derives the view from `page.url.hash`.

links.label: The system map's selected view is component state, not a derive of the hash

nodes.label: A system-map edge carries a kind, and its long label shows only on the edge you are on
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. every edge in the system map has a `kind` (flow, enforced, guarded, decision, foreign-key), the canvas strokes it and the legend names it by that kind, and the long condition label is drawn only on the edge under the pointer or focus instead of on every edge at once. The authored pipeline and path views stay hand-kept without a kind and the parser fills `flow`; the generated views set their own. `validateGraph` now fails an edge with no kind.

links.label: A system-map edge carries a kind, and its long label shows only on the edge you are on

nodes.label: A day insight is grounded in the facts and stored once per day
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. the Today page's insights card writes one short read per day, on request, from the day's logged planned sessions. Every figure in the reply must already appear in the facts the engine and the runner's own logs supplied; a reply that states any other number is dropped, the way a reworded reason is. The read is stored one row per user and date with a fingerprint of the day's logs, so a second visit shows the stored text and only a genuinely changed day is offered a fresh read. The card stays out of the way until every workout on the day is logged or skipped.

links.label: A day insight is grounded in the facts and stored once per day

nodes.label: A mid-week start opens with a short week, and the week floor follows the goal and the runner
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. a plan that starts after Monday opens with a genuinely short first week, pro-rated to the days left in the calendar week the runner started in (a Thursday start is four days, `firstWeekFraction`). Only the delivered first week is short; the ramp chains on the normal curve, so the next whole week is the plan it always was. The flat five-km weekly floor is replaced by a minimum derived from the goal and the runner's experience (`weekFloorKm`): a beginner on a short goal may run a genuinely short week, an experienced marathoner keeps a real one, and the floor never drops below one real run. A week too light to hold a long run and a second run becomes a single short easy run rather than a token jog, and a long run is not repeated verbatim by a rebuild when the approved first week is unrealistic. The rebuild returns a plain warning for that fallback, but it is not shown to the runner yet (the preview route reads only the weeks, and no path carries a rebuild or engine warning to a runner today), so surfacing it is a follow-up.

links.label: A mid-week start opens with a short week, and the week floor follows the goal and the runner

nodes.label: A session whose modality has no run is not framed as one
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. a mobility session's reason is about the mobility work, not a run. The deterministic composer names the area the session's own title carries ("Hips and glutes", "Hamstrings and calves") in its role line and, when the session is alone on its day, in its day line; it keeps the "pairs with the run you already have that day" line only when a run or strength session really shares the day. The rephrase prompt now carries each session's modality with a rule that a strength, mobility, walking or recovery session is not a run, so the model does not force a running frame on a line that has none.

links.label: A session whose modality has no run is not framed as one

nodes.label: A system-map node carries several links, not one
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. each system-map node carries a list of links, one for each place it points: its code, the test that guards it, the decision entry behind it and the pull request. Each link is a kind, a short label and a target. A node with no real target carries no links rather than a placeholder, and a link whose kind is unknown is a `doc` rather than a guess.

links.label: A system-map node carries several links, not one

nodes.label: Every prose model path is guarded for the writing rules and the sanitizer
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. every path where a model writes text a person reads must put `WRITING_RULES` in the prompt it sends and run the reply through `sanitizeText` before it is stored or shown. A scan test finds each prose model call and fails when one is missing them.

links.label: Every prose model path is guarded for the writing rules and the sanitizer

nodes.label: The load model may ease or hold, never build, and an eased week dips its long run
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. the fitness and fatigue load model can only lower a future week's volume intent to `ease` or `hold`. It never sets `build`, never writes a distance or pace, and an eased week also dips its long run, the way a deload does.

links.label: The load model may ease or hold, never build, and an eased week dips its long run

nodes.label: The ten percent weekly ceiling stays, and a week never exceeds its own target
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. the engine's roughly ten percent weekly step ceiling stays the load-bearing safety bound. The load model works inside it: its maximum ease is ten percent (`LOAD_DEFAULTS.maxEase`), and the applied plan's week never carries more prescribed volume than the engine's own target for that week.

links.label: The ten percent weekly ceiling stays, and a week never exceeds its own target

nodes.label: The plan-quality backtest asserts the invariants hard, not as expected failures
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. a backtest that records known engine bugs as expected failures is not merged. The plan-quality backtest generates the full goal matrix and asserts every hard invariant as a plain assertion, with no allowances, so a regression fails CI.

links.label: The plan-quality backtest asserts the invariants hard, not as expected failures

nodes.label: The load model defaults to shadow, and changing a plan is opt-in
nodes.note: 2026-11-26. every plan and adapt runs the load model in `shadow`, which records what it would change and applies nothing. The two modes that change a plan, `advisory` and `apply`, are opt-in per runner. `off` turns it off.

links.label: The load model defaults to shadow, and changing a plan is opt-in

nodes.label: The AI picks typed intents; the engine computes every number
nodes.note: 2026-11-25. every path that changes a plan goes through one pipeline. A model returns typed, confidence-scored decisions (volume intent, quality-day count, long-run delta), each an enum from a closed set, and the engine turns those into every distance and pace. A missing or out-of-set answer is dropped and the deterministic plan stands.

links.label: The AI picks typed intents; the engine computes every number

nodes.label: Jev runs through OpenRouter, with no separate TypeSafe key
nodes.note: 2026-11-25. the Jev decisions model (the coach safety classifier and the plan-change pipeline) is served through OpenRouter's decisions API on the existing `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Model id `typesafe/jev-1.14`, with `~typesafe/jev-latest` as the rolling alias. No `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`.

links.label: Jev runs through OpenRouter, with no separate TypeSafe key

nodes.label: The main session reads a subagent's diff before merging
nodes.note: 2026-11-25. the main session reads the changed code in every subagent PR before merging, and confirms three things: the change does what the brief asked, it does not weaken an existing test or assertion to pass, and any claim it makes about the research or data it cites actually holds in the code. A green CI gate is evidence, not a review.

views.title: Module by module
views.lede: Each module, what it computes and may decide, wired to the invariants and tests that hold it.

nodes.label: Plan engine
nodes.note: Computes: The phase arc, the weekly volume and long-run curve, VDOT paces, and every session's distance, pace and count. May decide: The phase shape and every number. Nothing here is model-authored.

nodes.label: Load model
nodes.note: Computes: Fitness, fatigue and form curves from the plan and the runner's logs, and a readiness score. May decide: To ease or hold a future week. Never to build, and never a number.

nodes.label: Plan-change pipeline
nodes.note: Computes: The typed, confidence-scored decisions (volume intent, quality-day count, long-run delta) and the mapping onto a week's shape. May decide: Which weeks change and by which typed intent. An out-of-set answer is dropped.

nodes.label: AI shaping pass
nodes.note: Computes: One bounded request per plan that asks the model for a quality kind and volume, strength and mobility intents. May decide: Nothing on its own. Every answer is validated, and the deterministic plan stands when it fails.

nodes.label: Session reason composer
nodes.note: Computes: Each session's and week's reason from the plan's own decisions, with no invented numbers. May decide: Which true sentences to include. A fact the plan does not carry is left out.

nodes.label: Reason rephrase gate
nodes.note: Computes: A gate that keeps a reworded reason only when it adds no number the deterministic reason did not have. May decide: Whether a reworded line is kept or dropped.

nodes.label: Session reason pass
nodes.note: Computes: The batched model call that rewords session reasons after a plan is saved, and the store step. May decide: Nothing about the plan. It replaces a reason's text only when the gate keeps it.

nodes.label: Adapt
nodes.note: Computes: Rebuilds only the weeks that have not started, seeded with real recent volume and feedback. May decide: The shape of the future weeks, inside the engine's own bounds.

nodes.label: Week-one rebuild
nodes.note: Computes: The rest of the plan from the runner's approved first week: its days, session types and added workouts. May decide: The pattern the later weeks follow. Week one itself is never touched here.

nodes.label: Schedule placing
nodes.note: Computes: Each session's start time inside the runner's saved windows, moving a session only when its own day cannot hold it. May decide: Only a day and a start time. No distance, volume or training maths.

nodes.label: VDOT paces
nodes.note: Computes: Training paces from a race time or an effective VDOT. May decide: Nothing. It is pure maths.

nodes.label: Onboarding suggestions
nodes.note: Computes: Recommended onboarding values, each with a plain reason. May decide: Nothing. It suggests a starting point.

nodes.label: Coach safety classifier
nodes.note: Computes: A typed risk read (none, caution, urgent) with a confidence, for a coach message. May decide: Whether to redirect on a confident, non-none risk. It never diagnoses.

nodes.label: Model router
nodes.note: Computes: Time-boxed model calls: Cloudflare Workers AI first, OpenRouter on error or timeout. May decide: Nothing. Callers decide, and every path degrades on failure.

nodes.label: Connection sync
nodes.note: Computes: Pulls new activities and daily health from a linked account and matches activities to planned sessions. May decide: Which activity matches which session, proposed until the runner confirms.

nodes.label: Connection security
nodes.note: Computes: Encrypted token storage and the signed OAuth state. May decide: Nothing. It stores and refreshes tokens.

nodes.label: Cron handlers
nodes.note: Computes: The nightly and weekly coach note, and the connection syncs. May decide: When the note and the syncs run.

nodes.label: Plan routes
nodes.note: Computes: Thin Hono handlers for generate, preview, adapt, rebuild, load and session state. May decide: It validates input and calls the pure logic. It holds no plan maths.

nodes.label: Admin surface
nodes.note: Computes: Reads metadata only: users, plans, the load model's shadow records, and app errors. May decide: Admin state and the audit trail. It never changes a plan's numbers.

nodes.label: Data model
nodes.note: Computes: The Drizzle tables, indexes and references. May decide: Nothing. It is the shape of what is stored.
